title: EPI-OrGenHm: A GPU-Accelerated Closed-Loop Framework for In Silico Perturbation Screening of Epigenetic Dynamics
content: We present EPI-OrGenHm (Epigenetic Ordered Gene Homeostasis) — a closed-loop computational framework integrating DNA methylation dynamics, gene expression regulation, virtual perturbation action, and entropy-based anomaly detection within a unified GPU-accelerated environment. The model is calibrated on public scNMT-seq data (GSE121690, 364 mouse cells, 43 genes, 9362 CpG sites) using a previously developed structural-entropy approach. The regulatory network combines STRING DB (functional interactions) and TRRUST (directed regulatory links). The key methodological innovation is the implementation of negative feedback in the "expression → methylation" loop, which stabilizes the system and prevents methylation collapse under virtual demethylating perturbation. A sigmoid age coordinate with a quadratic penalty for extreme hypomethylation is introduced for quantifying relative epigenetic state changes. Results (model coordinates): Under the current parameterization, the baseline model age coordinate is 95.7 a.u. The maximum reduction of this coordinate is 2.75 a.u. (to 92.96 a.u.) at perturbation strength S = 0.179. The model-predicted window with zero entropy-flagged dysregulation is S ∈ [0, 0.357]. Above S = 0.393, 1.3–1.9% of cells are flagged by the entropy-based classifier. A pronounced nonlinearity is observed: 20% of the maximum perturbation (S = 0.10) produces 88.4% of the maximum effect. Entropy analysis (Shannon, LZ-complexity, persistent entropy, KL-divergence, spatial entropy) confirms these metrics as sensitive markers of structural epigenetic changes. The OrGenHm metric is introduced as a theoretical lower bound (M̄ < 0.185) for catastrophic loss of ordered gene homeostasis; in the present simulations this bound is never reached, and early dysregulation is detected by entropy thresholds instead. EPI-OrGenHm enables statistically robust in silico screening of virtual perturbation regimes (n = 1000 cells per dose, CV of optimal strength < 5% across LOOCV folds) and generates hypotheses for target genes and parameter ranges. Michaelis–Menten fitting (R² = 0.696) with leave-one-dose-out cross-validation (RMSE = 0.575 a.u.) confirms ranking stability. All dose effects are statistically significant (p < 0.001, Bonferroni-corrected Welch's t-test, n = 1000).Scope statement: The model is calibrated on embryonic mouse cells and predicts relative changes in a model-specific epigenetic coordinate, not absolute human age or clinical outcomes. Translation to aging somatic tissue requires recalibration on aged-tissue data and experimental validation.
